title: Span
tagline: Call Span. Ask if you’ll make payroll. Watch the answer get made.

sections.inspiration: Small business owners make money decisions every day with no answer. 'Can I pay my people Friday?' lives in their books, spread across the bank balance, forty unpaid invoices, each customer's habits, and the bills due. Turning that into a yes or a no has always needed an accountant they can't afford, slower than they can wait. Intuit's challenge text named it: work that used to be too slow or costly to run. We wanted the owner to be able to ask out loud and watch the answer get made.
sections.what_it_does: Span is a phone number. You call or text it and ask 'am I making payroll Friday?' While it works, a web page draws its reasoning live as a workflow: pulling context, scoring every open invoice by that customer's payment history, forecasting cash on payday, the answer, the levers that close the gap, and the ask. Say yes and it texts the right customers, handles their replies, negotiates installments with the customer's agent under your rules, takes the payment through a pay link, and the gap on screen ticks down. At the end it generates a one-page report. The same assistant answers on ASI:One. Second question it handles: 'should I take this customer's order?'
sections.how_we_built_it: Data: Intuit's 100-company QuickBooks dataset flattened into Tiger Postgres (84k invoices, 144k payments, 26k payroll runs). Fast lane: a payment-behavior model (gradient-boosted trees, trained across all companies, last 60 days held out) predicts when each invoice pays and whether it ever will; Jev fills this role where available. Slow lane: Gemini plans, decides levers, writes the spoken answer, and writes the report. Reminders are drafted by Qwen3-1.7B fine-tuned on Veri from examples generated off the dataset. Every tool call is an event on a server-sent stream; the frontend (designed and built in Paper) renders those events as a workflow canvas with six node types. Photon is the phone number for calls, SMS, and customer replies. Fetch uAgents register the assistant and the simulated customer agents on Agentverse. Visa sandbox and Solana devnet are the pay rails. Sentry traces every request and model call. Devin built the loader and the pay page. Hosted on Vultr.
sections.company_challenges: Intuit: real-time analysis on the provided dataset, answering a question QuickBooks users can't get today. Fetch.ai / Agentverse: discoverable via ASI:One, turns intent into action, agent-to-agent negotiation. Photon: calling and messaging agent on one number. Visa: GenAI commerce with a secure sandbox payment closing the loop. Veri: fine-tuned open model used at runtime. Paper: the workflow canvas is the interface, designed in Paper. Cognition: Devin built two modules (session links attached). Sentry: Tracing + AI agent monitoring + Logs; bug write-up below. MLH: Gemini, Tiger Data, ElevenLabs, Vultr, Solana, GoDaddy domain. Model Learning track: learned payment-behavior model with held-out metrics and a fine-tuned drafter.
sections.built_with: python, fastapi, postgresql, tigerdata, gemini, scikit-learn, qwen, veri, uagents, fetch.ai, photon, visa, solana, elevenlabs, sentry, devin, vultr, paper
sections.disclosures: Customer agents in the demo are simulated from each customer's real payment history in the dataset. No dataset rows were modified.

sentry_bug_writeup.status: verified with local Sentry SDK trace; cloud upload pending DSN
sentry_bug_writeup.bug: Cash forecast excluded overdue unpaid bills by filtering due dates BETWEEN as_of and target.
sentry_bug_writeup.impact: Palletbay omitted four overdue liabilities totaling $1,598.55. The two-week expected payroll gap was incorrectly $0; corrected gap is $384.94.
sentry_bug_writeup.fix: Include unpaid bills issued by dataset as_of and due on or before target. A regression test checks the reconciled total of $10,866.86.
